_README: Hand-checked corrections to the automatic classification in build-manifest.mjs.
Keyed by applet name. Any of kind, status, ctkUrl and notes may be set; what is
set here always wins. Add an entry whenever you open an applet and find the
classifier got it wrong, in the same commit as the port.

Aliquot.notes: Ported to aliquot/. Opponent is AliquotCanvas.FindFactor verbatim; moves are buttons instead of a typed divisor.

LCGame.notes: Ported as carroll-logic. BSmartDiagram placement rules, TDumbDiagram Received/superfluity/CheckReturn from the bytecode; one syllogism instead of the 12-diagram sorites chain; contradictions reported. Method verified sound and complete on all 5,041 consistent cell premise pairs.

Kayles.notes: Ported as kayles (from the dawsons-kayles page). KaylesGame heaps/Play/GoodMove/MakeRandomMove and Reset from the bytecode; mex reproduces the 84-value table; period 12 from 71 checked to 400; full circle is a second-player win for 3..60.

JEuclidGame.notes: Ported as euclid-game. RecordMove/Play/IsOver from the bytecode (the computer has no strategy). Checked on all 10,296 pairs from 1..144: every game ends with the multiples of gcd up to max, in max/gcd - 2 moves.

JChangingColors.notes: Ported as changing-colors. Reset, the four arrow families, Take back, numbers view and the hint cells from the bytecode. Checked by GF(2) elimination: one colour is unreachable for N=4,6,8 (hint invariant) and also 5,7 (other invariants); only 3x3 is solvable.

Jam.notes: Ported as jam. Map, masks, bestMove (with its 1-in-10 mistakes) from the bytecode. Checked: cities = tic-tac-toe lines, magic table = Lo Shu (Fif). The mistake-free computer is still beatable (forks): always moving first, and after its openings on roads 1 and 3.

IntIter.notes: Ported as ducci. Compute/Undo/Reset/Random and the +/-1 halves from the bytecode; starts with Random ticked. Checked: N=4 and powers of 2 die out; N=5 '3 or 6' holds (exact 15); N=6 'loops of 2 and 3' is really 6 and 3 (2 and 1 up to turns).

Hounds.notes: Ported as hare-hounds. Rules from the applet's Board class; the applet is Robert Kirkland's Hare and Hounds 2.0, all rights reserved, so the opponent is an original exact solver (hounds win with best play, within 23 moves).

Horse.notes: Already ported as four-knights (hand-made original): both SimpleGames/Horse.shtml and Curriculum/Games/FourKnights.shtml embed this applet. The port has the applet's unfolded ring and its Hint (square numbers).

HexTheory.notes: Ported as hex-draw. CellCell's chain search and neighbour tables from the bytecode (same chain shown); 8-grid shows both chains. Gale's walk written from the page. Checked: no draws on hex/6-grid, 4-grid draws = 8-grid double wins (duality).

Hex7.notes: Ported as hex7. Rules from the applet (7x7, White first, centre blocked on move 1, Basic/Advanced). The applet is Robert Kirkland's Hex 2.0, all rights reserved, so its AI is not transcribed: the opponent is an original Monte Carlo player.

Hanoi3c.notes: Ported as hanoi-3c. Anderson's GATHER/SHIFT/SPREAD from the bytecode. Goal is the page's (three whole single-colour towers, deranged); the applet's CompleteDerangement accepted mixed piles. BFS: fewest 5/22/62 vs algorithm 10/38/102; all six PERMUTE orders work, contrary to the page's guess.

hanoi.notes: Ported as hanoi. The sitemap match pointed at exchange/hanoi.shtml, a reader's letter; the applet page is recurrence/hanoi.shtml. Solution() and Help() (Zylla) from the bytecode; Help is optimal from all 3^n positions up to n=8.

guess.notes: Ported as whats-next. All nine guesscanvas rules match the bytecode for every parameter; quirks kept: AP start and difference in -11..0, 'Shifted powers' shift always 0. Census: 2,673 distinct sequences, none with two answers.

Grundy.notes: Ported as grundy. Computer is GrundyCanvas.Play/MakeGoodMove/MakeRandomMove verbatim, heap order included; the hard-coded NimValue table (0-39) and the page's table (0-59) both match the mex rule.

FrogsAndToads.notes: Ported as frogs-toads. Frogs on the left as on the cut-the-knot page (the applet drew toad.gif there). Exhaustive check: two solutions only when both sides have 2+ animals (Fibonacci many with a lone animal); hole string palindromic iff N+M even, not only M=N as the page says.

FrogsAndToads2D.notes: Ported as frogs-toads-2d. The jar also carries the 1-D puzzle's rules as its single-row and single-column cases.

DominoCovering.notes: Ported as domino-faults. The page is about fault lines, and the applet checks exactly that: CheckFinished() wants N*M/2 dominoes and every interior line crossed.

BiColorHanoi.notes: Ported as bicolor-hanoi. The applet sets up the bicolor position but its win test and par (2^N-1) are leftovers from the single-tower Hanoi applet it was built from, so the goal comes from the cut-the-knot page instead: both towers monochrome and swapped.

Diagonals.notes: Ported as diagonals. The page is titled "Diagonal Count"; it is a counting experiment, but it has a win condition (n-3 diagonals drawn) so the classifier's "game" stands.

BarryCipra.notes: Ported as stones-in-cups. The page calls it "Stones in Cups"; the applet is named after Barry Cipra, who set the problem.

DawsonKayles.notes: Ported to dawsons-kayles/. Grundy values recomputed with the mex rule and checked against the applet's hard-coded 137; heaps() joins a wrap-around run before dropping lone skittles, which the applet did the other way round.

Hanoing.notes: Ported as hanoing. The Tower of Hanoi disguised as a row of coloured squares.

FractionGame.notes: Ported to fraction-game/ as Contorted Fractions. Opponent is the applet's greedy SuggestMove/IsThereWorthyMove; Legal() forgot to require an integer replacement for an integer, which is fixed so the game terminates.

Tromino.notes: Filed under Curriculum/Geometry but it is a real tiling puzzle: the archive has TrominoBoard and TrominoPiece.

Tromino2.notes: As Tromino: the deficient-board tiling puzzle, not a static diagram.

SierpinskiChaosGame.notes: The 'chaos game' is an algorithm you watch run, not a game you win.

ChessTournament.notes: Probability demonstration; Canvas and Panel only, no move or score model.

ArithMagic.notes: Arithmetic magic trick; no page found in the sitemap, so ctkUrl is unresolved.

Cardi.notes: Cardioid construction (CTKCycloid classes), not a card game - the name misleads the classifier.

FourPegs.notes: Ported as four-pegs. The applet's 30x30 grid and side range 1..20 are scaled to 12x12 and 1..4 so the points are tappable; the puzzle is scale-invariant.

Coin.notes: A single Coin.class shared widget, not a standalone applet.
